Card.description: Root of every rendered UI — children stack vertically inside one card in the chat. Keep it to two or three blocks: this sits in a narrow chat rail, under a message that has already done the explaining.

Text.description: A line or paragraph of prose. style: 'title' a small section heading · 'strong' emphasis · 'muted' a quiet aside · 'body' (default). Use ONE short Text to frame a decision — the chat message above already carries your explanation, so do not repeat it here.

Callout.description: A tinted banner for something the user must notice before choosing: a cost, an overwrite warning, a blocked prerequisite, a render that will take minutes. Use 'danger' only for destructive or irreversible consequences.

OptionList.description: THE default way to ask the author to choose — an inset card of Option rows separated by hairlines. Use it for 2–6 choices that need more than a bare label: models, durations, takes, drafts, characters to add, next steps. header: a small uppercase label above the card. footnote: one quiet line beneath it (e.g. 'Or just tell me what you want instead.'). select: 'one' (default) — a tap picks that item and sends immediately. 'many' — taps toggle, and nothing is sent until the confirm button — use 'many' whenever the author may legitimately want SEVERAL of the listed things (which speakers to add to the World, which takes to keep). send: REQUIRED when select is 'many': the lead of the composed message, to which the picked items' `send` values are appended after a colon — e.g. send "Add these characters to the World" + picks "Miles", "Vera" posts "Add these characters to the World: Miles, Vera". Ignored when select is 'one'. confirm: the confirm button's label when select is 'many' (default "Continue"). Ignored when select is 'one'.

Option.description: One choice in an OptionList, rendered as a tappable row. title: the choice. send: the message sent AS THE USER when this is picked — write it as the user would ('Use the second reference'), never as an instruction to yourself. It MUST OPEN WITH the words shown on the control itself (its title/label), because this message is the author's ONLY confirmation that the row they hit is the row they meant; put any extra brief AFTER that opening — title 'Punch up the dialogue' ⇒ send 'Punch up the dialogue — sharpen the voices in the audition scene', never send 'Let me tighten those lines'. subtitle: one line of why-you'd-pick-this. meta: a short right-aligned qualifier ("~40s", "12 credits", "shot03"). image: a thumbnail URL for the row's leading badge. badge: a tiny pill ("Recommended", "Current"). selected: marks the option already in force. tone 'danger' for a destructive choice.

MediaGrid.description: A grid of image thumbnails — the RIGHT way to ask which reference, still, take or character sheet to use. ALWAYS prefer this over listing image URLs as markdown. Tapping a thumbnail opens it FULL-SCREEN for a proper look; picking is a separate explicit control, so the author can inspect before committing. columns: 2 (default) or 3; use 3 only for six or more small thumbnails. select: 'one' (default) — a tap picks that item and sends immediately. 'many' — taps toggle, and nothing is sent until the confirm button — use 'many' when several images are legitimately wanted (a multi-reference generation). send: REQUIRED when select is 'many': the lead of the composed message, to which the picked items' `send` values are appended after a colon — e.g. send "Add these characters to the World" + picks "Miles", "Vera" posts "Add these characters to the World: Miles, Vera". Ignored when select is 'one'. confirm: the confirm button's label when select is 'many' (default "Continue"). Ignored when select is 'one'.

MediaItem.description: One pickable image in a MediaGrid. src: the image URL (a /storyboard-media, /library or generation URL from the tools — never invent one). send: the message sent AS THE USER when this is picked — write it as the user would ('Use the second reference'), never as an instruction to yourself. It MUST OPEN WITH the words shown on the control itself (its title/label), because this message is the author's ONLY confirmation that the row they hit is the row they meant; put any extra brief AFTER that opening — title 'Punch up the dialogue' ⇒ send 'Punch up the dialogue — sharpen the voices in the audition scene', never send 'Let me tighten those lines'; in a 'many' grid make it a NOUN PHRASE instead ("the dawn clearing"), because the picks are joined into one sentence. label: a short name under the thumbnail. caption: one extra line of context. selected: marks the current pick.

AudioList.description: A stack of playable audio rows — THE way to hand finished audio back to the author: a Seed Audio scene, radio takes, new sound versions. The author plays each clip right in the chat; NEVER paste an audio URL as a markdown link instead. Playing never sends anything — picking is a separate control that appears only on rows given a `send`, so a listen-only card is simply rows without one. select: 'one' (default) — a tap picks that item and sends immediately. 'many' — taps toggle, and nothing is sent until the confirm button — use 'many' when several takes can be kept. send: REQUIRED when select is 'many': the lead of the composed message, to which the picked items' `send` values are appended after a colon — e.g. send "Add these characters to the World" + picks "Miles", "Vera" posts "Add these characters to the World: Miles, Vera". Ignored when select is 'one'. confirm: the confirm button's label when select is 'many' (default "Continue"). Ignored when select is 'one'.

AudioItem.description: One playable clip in an AudioList, rendered as a row with an inline play button. src: the audio URL (a /sound-media or generation URL a tool returned — never invent one). title: what the clip is ("Take 2 — heavier rain"). send: OPTIONAL — give it only when picking this clip is a real decision; then it follows the usual rules (the message sent AS THE USER when this is picked — write it as the user would ('Use the second reference'), never as an instruction to yourself. It MUST OPEN WITH the words shown on the control itself (its title/label), because this message is the author's ONLY confirmation that the row they hit is the row they meant; put any extra brief AFTER that opening — title 'Punch up the dialogue' ⇒ send 'Punch up the dialogue — sharpen the voices in the audition scene', never send 'Let me tighten those lines'; in a 'many' list a NOUN PHRASE instead). Omit send entirely when the card is just for listening. subtitle: one line of context (what changed in this take). meta: a short right-aligned qualifier ("12s", "v3"). badge: a tiny pill ("Liked", "New"). selected: marks the take already in force.

Recommendation.description: A single recommended course of action, presented as a hero card with one big call-to-action button. Use it when you have ONE thing to propose and want a clean yes — a render you're about to submit, a plan you'd run next, a draft you'd pin. title: the proposal. body: two sentences of why. send: the message sent AS THE USER when this is picked — write it as the user would ('Use the second reference'), never as an instruction to yourself. It MUST OPEN WITH the words shown on the control itself (its title/label), because this message is the author's ONLY confirmation that the row they hit is the row they meant; put any extra brief AFTER that opening — title 'Punch up the dialogue' ⇒ send 'Punch up the dialogue — sharpen the voices in the audition scene', never send 'Let me tighten those lines' (the go-ahead). cta: the button text ("Render it", "Do it") — default "Continue". bullets: up to 4 short supporting facts. image: a preview thumbnail. meta: cost/duration ("~90s · 12 credits").

Compare.description: Two or three options weighed side by side on identical rows — models, providers, takes, drafts. Use it only when the choice genuinely turns on comparing the SAME attributes; a plain OptionList reads better for everything else. Never more than 3 columns: the chat rail is narrow.

Column.description: One side of a Compare. label: what this column is ("Seedance", "Veo 3.1"). rows: the same {label, value} keys IN THE SAME ORDER as every other column, so they line up. badge: a tiny pill ("Recommended"). send: the message sent AS THE USER when this is picked — write it as the user would ('Use the second reference'), never as an instruction to yourself. It MUST OPEN WITH the words shown on the control itself (its title/label), because this message is the author's ONLY confirmation that the row they hit is the row they meant; put any extra brief AFTER that opening — title 'Punch up the dialogue' ⇒ send 'Punch up the dialogue — sharpen the voices in the audition scene', never send 'Let me tighten those lines' — supply it to make the whole column pickable.

KeyValue.description: A compact label/value detail block — the parameters of a render you're about to submit, a shot's settings, a cut's stats. Pair it with Actions to make a confirmation.

Steps.description: An ordered plan, numbered, shown BEFORE you run a multi-step pipeline so the author can see what's coming. steps: {title, detail?, meta?}. current: index of the step in progress (0-based) — omit when nothing has started yet.

Chips.description: A row of small follow-up pills. Tapping one sends its label verbatim as the user's next message, so write each as something the AUTHOR would say ('Show me the other takes'). Use for cheap side-quests offered alongside the main choice — never as the main choice itself.

Actions.description: A group of buttons — the plain yes/no/other choice. direction: 'row' (default) for two or three short labels, 'column' when the labels are sentences.

Action.description: One button. label: the button text. send: the message sent AS THE USER when this is picked — write it as the user would ('Use the second reference'), never as an instruction to yourself. It MUST OPEN WITH the words shown on the control itself (its title/label), because this message is the author's ONLY confirmation that the row they hit is the row they meant; put any extra brief AFTER that opening — title 'Punch up the dialogue' ⇒ send 'Punch up the dialogue — sharpen the voices in the audition scene', never send 'Let me tighten those lines'. Exactly ONE action in a group should be 'primary'. tone 'danger' for destructive or irreversible choices (overwrite, delete, regenerate over existing work).

Section.description: A titled group of blocks, separated from its neighbours by a rule. Only reach for it when one card genuinely carries two distinct groups (e.g. 'The references' and 'What I'd do'); a single-section card should skip it and put the blocks straight in the Card.
